scope: User question -> predefined intent -> original source content -> citation-backed answer (reject changed/absent source); no private files, no LLM reasoning claims

cases.title: Original observation formula meaning
cases.answer: The original TAIRID Math passage writes O = Tᵃ · Iᵇ, defines O as projected stable structure rather than perception, and explicitly says a and b describe recursive depth rather than ordinary numeric powers. Other author passages use power-like mathematical operations, so a fully executable numeric interpretation remains unapproved. This is an author-theory interpretation, not an independently established physics law.

evidence.needle: The exponents a and b denote not power in a numeric sense
time (T) does not represent a clock or a metric.

cases.title: SDR is not a validated truth oracle
cases.answer: The author wrote a weighted root mean square SDR formula in the translation manuscript. The Infinite Library manuscript separately states that SDR is not a truth detector and proposes using it to track unresolved epistemic disagreement. The residual calculation can be defined only after measurable outputs, references, weights, units and their error assumptions are specified; the proposed universal epistemic interpretation is not independently calibrated.

evidence.needle: SDR is not a truth detector.

cases.title: Retained structure requires test of later reuse
cases.answer: The Kernel's original simulation review reports that reaching a target once was insufficient to demonstrate useful stable form. A corrected two-phase model checked formation and subsequent reuse, and found that residue can become stale or lock systems. This is source-reported model evidence in its stated setup, not an established universal physical memory equation.

evidence.needle: What failed: treating all retained form as useful memory.
What failed: single-phase success as a measure of stable form.
What survived: two-phase viability - formation plus reuse

cases.title: Three gates admit attempts but do not prove physics
cases.answer: The source defines bandwidth, orientation and phase windows and intersects them into a period in which a merge is allowed to be attempted. Permitting an attempt is not evidence that it succeeds or that a microscopic physical interaction changes. Any physical extrapolation needs independent measurement and a domain-specific law.

evidence.needle: only there are you even allowed to try the merge.

cases.title: Generic golden/Fibonacci attractor failed kernel test
cases.answer: The Kernel review explicitly reports a failed generic branching/β golden-ratio attractor. Fibonacci-like patterns appeared under narrower spatial packing conditions, not as a universal adaptive-balance law. The negative control must remain available in the working Library.

evidence.needle: What failed: phi as a generic branching or beta attractor.
What survived: Fibonacci-like structure belongs to constrained spatial recurrence and packing

cases.title: Native Shannon entropy method and limitations
cases.answer: Shannon discrete entropy is mathematically defined as H(X) = −Σ p(x) log₂ p(x) for a normalized discrete probability distribution. Its output is in bits. This is distinct from thermodynamic entropy in J/K and from TAIRID's separate structural meaning of information; no automatic conversion is permitted. The present reference record is source-anchored but still requires item-level citation review.

evidence.needle: does not refer to stored data, bits, or Shannon-style informational probability.
